title: wc_crypto2dev_cleanup while streaming hash in flight leaks HashCtx
description: Scenario that triggers: caller initializes a wc_Sha256 with WOLF_CRYPTO2DEV_DEVID, calls wc_Sha256Update (allocates Crypto2DevHashCtx, stores in sha->devCtx), then calls wc_crypto2dev_cleanup() before calling wc_Sha256Final(). Cleanup unregisters the callback and closes pool slots (closing the in-flight op_fd). Later, wc_Sha256Free(&sha) is called but the callback is no longer registered, so crypto2dev_free_hash() is never invoked, and the Crypto2DevHashCtx heap allocation at sha->devCtx is leaked. The maintenance consequence: every user who structures their code as 'cleanup in a destructor or signal handler' while streaming will hit a leak. The header says cleanup must be called after all ops complete, but this constraint is not enforced. Filed as burden rather than a test/doc gap because the failure mode is silent and the ordering requirement is easy to violate.
